Dear Sir/Madam,
Re: Joshua Vance, DOB: 17/11/2013

I am writing this letter to refer you Joshua, a three-month old infant, who is complaining of constipation
and mild dehydration. Your urgent assessment would be highly appreciated.

Joshua's mother had a normal vaginal delivery at 38 weeks gestation and she has no history of perinatal or
neonatal complications. His birth weight was 3250 g.

Upon the first two visits, Joshua's mother was concerned that her son had only one bowel action every
three-days as well as breastfeeding issues. Moreover, she mentioned that he wake up crying at night and
he pulls his legs up to his chest every half hour. On examination, his weight increased to 4200 g and had
hard faeces on his abdomen. Thus, he was commenced on a trial of Coloxyl drops daily and two bottles of
milk mixed with water.

Today, his mother reported that her son had no bowel action in the last 5 days and he refused to feed as
well as he vomited once. On examination, he was mildly dehydrated as he had dry mucous membrane,
tissue turgor. However, normal capillary refill. Furthermore, his abdomen showed mild generalised
tenderness. Nonetheless, no guarding or rebound tenderness. In addition, his weight decreased to 4100 g.
